raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Follow-up to #46955.

- With `--engram-config` `lookup` `auto` (the default) and the tables in GPU memory (the default), each rank now reads its tokens' Engram rows in place from the owning GPU, as `peer_read` does, when the TP group is one NVLink domain: one node with full NVLink, or one multi-node NVLink fabric such as GB300 NVL72. Otherwise `auto` keeps picking a collective. The choice is one more branch of `resolve_engram_config`, the single place `auto` is resolved since #46955, and the log says `Engram lookup auto -> peer_read`.
- `custom_all_reduce_utils.in_one_nvlink_domain`: the topology check, built from the existing NVLink helpers; the physical-GPU-id gather moves out of `can_use_custom_all_reduce_with_nvlink` into `gather_physical_device_ids` so both use it.
- Docs: `auto` and its measurements.

Behavior change: default DeepSeek-V4.1 deployments with TP > 1 over NVLink allocate the Engram shards through CUDA VMM and map their peers' shards at load, instead of running a collective per Engram layer per step. The shard per GPU is the same size. Host tables and explicit `lookup` values are unchanged.

## Measurements

One Engram layer, GPU tables, slowest rank, us per layer. Decode is replayed from a CUDA graph.

DP attention 8, `all_to_all` (what `auto` ran before) against `peer_read`:

| Case | GB300 a2a (us) | GB300 peer (us) | B300 a2a (us) | B300 peer (us) | H200 a2a (us) | H200 peer (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 1K tokens per rank | 770 | 124 | 414 | 56 | 305 | 65 |
| prefill 8K | 731 | 200 | 476 | 158 | 619 | 204 |
| prefill 32K | 1,541 | 554 | 1,421 | 504 | 2,050 | 684 |
| decode 1 token per rank (B300) | | | 38.8 | 9.7 | | |
| decode 16 | 47.7 | 9.8 | 48.9 | 11.5 | 33.5 | 5.7 |
| decode 1,024 | 92.4 | 23.1 | 98.5 | 25.5 | 105.7 | 27.2 |

GB300 DP 8 runs on two 4-GPU nodes of one NVL72 rack.

DP attention 16 and 32 on GB300 (the hash columns do not divide, so the collectives are the all-reduce and reduce-scatter):

| Case | DP16 reduce-scatter (us) | DP16 peer (us) | DP32 reduce-scatter (us) | DP32 peer (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 1K | 811 | 128 | 1,333 | 119 |
| prefill 32K | 15,552 | 559 | 31,216 | 567 |
| decode 16 | 76 | 10.3 | 118 | 10.0 |
| decode 1,024 | 569 | 24.1 | 1,119 | 24.3 |

Plain TP (no DP attention), all-reduce against `peer_read`:

| Case | B300 TP2 AR (us) | B300 TP2 peer (us) | B300 TP8 AR (us) | B300 TP8 peer (us) | GB300 TP8 AR (us) | GB300 TP8 peer (us) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| prefill 1K tokens | 97.7 | 47.5 | 138.0 | 133.8 | 245.7 | 119.3 |
| prefill 32K | 1,208.8 | 393.0 | 1,559.4 | 527.5 | 1,566.7 | 500.3 |
| decode 1 | | | 13.4 | 9.3 | | |
| decode 16 | 10.9 | 9.9 | 16.7 | 12.3 | 17.2 | 9.7 |
| decode 1,024 | 45.8 | 20.8 | 65.3 | 25.7 | 65.6 | 22.7 |

Every collective and `peer_read` returned the same rows (bitwise across lookups in one process under DP attention; equal output checksums across processes under plain TP).

## Verification

- B300, default `--engram-config` at TP 8 and TP 2: the layer builds peer shards, and the output checksums match the explicit `peer_read` run (TP 8) and the all-reduce run (TP 2).
- Unit tests: `test/registered/unit/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py`, `test_parallel_state.py`, `test/registered/unit/layers/test_engram_history.py` pass.

 | `placement` | Where do the rows live? | `gpu` (default): device memory. `cpu`: pinned host memory, which the GPU reads in place; the HBM goes to the KV cache. |
 | `replication` | How many copies are there? | `none` (default): one table, its rows split across the TP group. `per_node`: each node holds the whole table, mapped by all of its ranks. |
-| `lookup` | How does a rank get rows another rank holds? Only with `replication` `none`. | `auto` (default): a collective SGLang picks for each step. `all_reduce`, `reduce_scatter`, `all_to_all`: that collective (see below). `peer_read`: each rank reads its tokens' rows straight from the owning GPU's shard over NVLink, with no collective. |
+| `lookup` | How does a rank get rows another rank holds? Only with `replication` `none`. | `auto` (default): `peer_read` for GPU tables whose TP group is one NVLink domain, otherwise a collective SGLang picks for each step. `all_reduce`, `reduce_scatter`, `all_to_all`: that collective (see below). `peer_read`: each rank reads its tokens' rows straight from the owning GPU's shard over NVLink, with no collective. |
 
 The configuration is logged at startup as `DeepSeek-V4.1 Engram tables: ...`, and the lookup
 `auto` resolves to, once the model is built, as `Engram lookup auto -> ...`.
 
 ```bash
-# Default: rows split across the TP group in GPU memory.
+# Default: rows split across the TP group in GPU memory; over NVLink, each rank reads its
+# tokens' rows from the owning GPU.
 sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp-size 4
 
 # Rows in host memory, one shard per rank: frees the HBM for the KV cache.
 sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp-size 4 \
   --engram-config '{"placement": "cpu"}'
-
-# Rows in GPU memory, read from the owning GPU without a collective.
-sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tp-size 8 --attn-dp-size 8 \
-  --engram-config '{"lookup": "peer_read"}'
 ```
 
 ## Choosing a configuration
 
 - **Small TP groups that are short of KV cache** (TP2, TP4, DP attention over 2 GPUs): use
   `{"placement": "cpu"}`. On GPU, each rank would hold half or a quarter of the 189 GiB.
-- **Wide TP groups** (8 GPUs and more, including DP attention across nodes): the shard per GPU is
-  small, and `{"lookup": "peer_read"}` removes the collective that each Engram layer otherwise
-  runs per step, a cost that grows with the group size.
-- **Latency-bound serving with memory to spare**: the default keeps every lookup in device memory.
+- **Wide TP groups and memory to spare** (8 GPUs and more, including DP attention across nodes):
+  the default. The shard per GPU is small, and over NVLink each rank reads its rows in place,
+  with no collective.
+
+## How `auto` picks
+
+With the tables in GPU memory, CUDA, and a TP group that is one NVLink domain (one node with
+full NVLink, or one multi-node NVLink fabric such as GB300 NVL72), `auto` reads the rows in
+place, as `peer_read` does, and logs `Engram lookup auto -> peer_read`. Measured with
+one Engram layer, it was faster than every collective, for prefill (1K to 32K tokens per rank)
+and decode (1 to 1,024 tokens per rank, in CUDA graphs):
+
+- DP attention 8 on GB300 (two nodes), B300 and H200: 2.8-7.5x faster than `all_to_all`.
+- DP attention 16 and 32 on GB300: 6-75x faster than the all-reduce and reduce-scatter, the only
+  collectives there.
+- Plain TP 2 and 8 on B300, TP 8 on GB300: up to 3.7x faster than the all-reduce, and never
+  slower.
 
-## How `auto` picks the collective
+Otherwise (host tables, or GPUs without NVLink between them) it picks a collective.
 
 Under DP attention, every rank needs rows for its own tokens, but each table is split across the
 TP group. The lookup gathers every rank's hash ids, looks up rows, and exchanges them:

-  fabric handles across an NVLink domain). Each GPU holds `1 / tp_size` of the table. With TP1
-  there is no peer, and the setting has no effect.
